newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures pare losses to end flat.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures pare losses to end flat.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Thursday"s TIFFE day session flat.
Turnover for the day session was 35,038, up from 8,190 on Wednesday.

The December contract fell to an intraday low of 99.22 in the morning following a decline in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, but pared losses in the afternoon as JGB futures rose into the positive territory, traders said.
The key March JGB futures contract closed up 0.17 at its intraday high of 126.34, after falling as low as 125.96 earlier.
"Euroyen futures moved within a narrow range, tracking JGB futures," said a city bank trader.
The Tokyo stock market"s failure to extend gains in the afternoon also helped to provide some support to the market, traders said.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended up 278.10 points, or 1.51 percent, at 18,688.06, after rising as high as 18,854.76.
"As the downside for JGB futures is seen limited, Euroyen futures are unlikely to fall much in the coming sessions," said a trust bank trader.
Traders said JGB futures were supported by short covering.
"December Euroyen futures are likely to remain stuck in a range between 99.20 and 99.25," the city bank trader said.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.50 percent, up from 0.49 percent on Wednesday.
The BOJ injected a net 100 billion yen into the money market on Thursday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
The overnight call rate edged higher due to fund-raising demand ahead of the end of the current reserve maintenance period on Friday, money traders said.
About 90 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.54 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
Two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent. One-month CDs were offered at 0.52 percent. Both rates were unchanged from Wednesday. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
